title: peer_whitelist doc claims DNSBL/FCrDNS bypass but neither is implemented
description: config.rs:45-47 and session.rs:189-190: the doc comment and inline comment both state the whitelist bypasses 'DNSBL, FCrDNS, and greylisting.' None of these three subsystems exist in the codebase. The flag currently only logs a line and does nothing else. Advertising a bypass guarantee for unimplemented behavior misleads operators reading the config docs and maintainers who must later wire up the flag. Mitigation: narrow the doc to describe what the flag actually does today, and call out the future hookup explicitly.
notes: SEC7 calibration: downgraded P1→P2. The doc is operator-visible and present-tense misleading (config.rs:45-47 says 'bypass DNSBL, FCrDNS, and greylisting' as a current guarantee; none of those subsystems exist). The log line 'spam filters bypassed' fires on connection, making the bypass appear to work. However, this is pre-release code with no shipped operators. No production harm today, but the inaccuracy is real. Comparable to 1onm.16 (maintainer-burden). True P1 requires a correctness failure or security gap in live code; this is a doc accuracy problem.
